-89.65820,39.80940.name: Southern Illinois University School of Medicine Fertility and IVF Center
-89.65820,39.80940.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: J. Ricardo Loret de Mola, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-81.09780,32.05905.name: Savannah Care Center
-81.09780,32.05905.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-2.88704,43.29077.name: CIC bioGUNE
-2.88704,43.29077.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.14765,51.52100.name: Fertility Plus
-0.14765,51.52100.state: Fertility Plus, 92 Harley Street, London, W1G 7HY
-0.14765,51.52100.company: Satellite clinic to Care Fertility London
-0.14765,51.52100.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to Care Fertility London. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

4.39750,51.21245.name: The Institute of Tropical Medicine (ITM)
4.39750,51.21245.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by The Institute of Tropical Medicine (ITM). It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on human health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

77.23000,28.61200.name: Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals
77.23000,28.61200.state: New Delhi — Ministry of Fisheries, Krishi Bhawan
77.23000,28.61200.desc: India’s regulator for animal experimentation, which has banned the use of animals for cosmetics testing and for some educational purposes. Restrictions here apply to a research system serving 1.4 billion people and rarely enter English-language discussion of animal research policy.

-122.53110,37.97350.name: Revive & Restore — black-footed ferret cloning
-122.53110,37.97350.desc: The cloned ferrets were produced from cells frozen in 1988 from an animal with no living descendants, returning genetic variation that the surviving population had lost entirely. It is the first case of cloning used to address inbreeding in an endangered species rather than to recreate an extinct one, and the material existed only because somebody banked it thirty years earlier.

5.94800,49.50400.name: Eurofins Scientific
5.94800,49.50400.desc: The largest food and feed testing network in the world, and the default commercial laboratory for GMO detection. Whether a shipment is found to contain engineered material usually depends on a test run here, which makes a private testing company the practical enforcement mechanism for labelling rules across Europe and beyond. One arrangement shows how a national standard travels. Its GeneScan arm is the exclusive North American licensee of the Japanese company FASMAC to run the Japanese Standard Methods — the methods Japanese agencies themselves use, developed by FASMAC with a consortium of Japanese food companies and two ministries. An exporter in the United States can therefore buy, from a private laboratory, a test performed identically to the one a Japanese regulator would perform, before shipping. The regulatory boundary is crossed by a licence between two companies.
